titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Abraham, Melchizedek and the Blind Jew (ch. 105)
part: ch. 105 — Abraham, Melchizedek and the Blind Jew
about: The author, arguing against a Jewish reader, says that Abraham and the prophets were justified by faith in the coming of Christ. In a reported dialogue God sends Abraham to Melchizedek at Salem, where bread and wine prefigure the Eucharist; the chapter ends by rebuking the blind Jew with Isaiah's words.

sentences.i: Chapter 105: Concerning the Faith of Abraham
sentences.n: Chapter heading. አሚነ is the construct state of አሚን 'faith' (from አምነ 'believe'; the construct ending -ä is the same as the accusative's, which is why the known entry says accusative), so 'faith-of Abraham', 'concerning Abraham's faith'. በእንተ 'concerning' is followed by a construct chain, as in the pilot's heading በእንተ ክብረ ነገሥት.

sentences.t: ወአንተሰ ፡ ኢትሌቡ ፡ ከመ ፡ በአሚን ፡ ይጸድቁ ፡ ከመ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ወዳዊት ፡ ወኵሎሙ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ በበ ፡ መትልው ፡ እለ ፡ ተነበዩ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ ለወልደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ።
sentences.l: And-as-for-you not-you-understand(?) that by-faith they-are-justified, like Abraham and-David and-all-of-them prophets, each succession(?), who they-prophesied concerning his-coming of-the-son-of God.
sentences.i: And you do not understand that they are made righteous by faith, as Abraham and David and all the prophets were, each in his own turn (?), who prophesied about the coming of the Son of God.
sentences.n: ወአንተሰ: ወ- 'and' + አንተ 'you (ms)' + emphatic -ሰ 'as for'. ኢትሌቡ (?) is read as a 2nd-person plural negative of ለበወ 'understand'; the regular spelling would be ኢትለብዉ (compare ኢይለብዉ in the last unit), so this form is irregular and the reading uncertain, and the singular አንተ with a plural verb is odd. There is no question particle (-ኑ), so I give a plain statement 'you do not understand'; a rhetorical question is possible but is not marked. ይጸድቁ is 3mp subjunctive of ጸድቀ 'be righteous, justified' after ከመ. በበ መትልው (?): distributive በበ 'each' + መትልው, which I take as an m-noun from ተልወ 'follow' (maqtəl type), 'succession, one following another' ('each in his turn'); the form and the sense are a guess. ወኵሎሙ ነቢያት: ኵሎሙ 'all of them' (ኵሉ + -ሙ) with ነቢያት in apposition. እለ ተነበዩ 'who prophesied' (ተነበየ, tä-stem of n-b-y). ምጽአቱ ለወልደ እግዚኣብሔር: the suffix -ሁ of ምጽአቱ anticipates the possessor, which ለ- introduces ('his coming, of the Son of God'); ወልደ is construct 'son-of'. Here the writer, arguing against a Jewish interlocutor, claims the patriarchs were justified by faith in the coming Christ.

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ በመዋዕልየኑ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ትፌኑ ፡ ቃልከ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ምድር ፤
sentences.l: And-said Abraham, 'In-my-days-is-it(?), O-Lord, will-you-send(?) your-word upon earth?'
sentences.i: And Abraham said, 'O Lord, in my days will you send your word upon the earth?'
sentences.n: The speaker shifts here: from the author addressing the Jew to a reported dialogue between Abraham and God. በመዋዕልየኑ: በ- 'in' + መዋዕል 'days' + -የ 'my' + -ኑ, the interrogative enclitic (it makes the question; it does not mean 'indeed'), so a question about 'in my days'; the word as a whole is uncertain (?). ትፌኑ (?) read as 2ms imperfect of ፈነወ 'send' (a III-w verb, whose imperfect I recall as ይፌኑ; from memory, unchecked); this -ኑ is part of the verb, not the question particle, which stands on the previous word. It could also be a statement 'you will send'. ቃልከ 'your word' is the Word of God, i.e. Christ, in the author's reading. The exchange is not from Genesis; it is the author's own expansion.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አልቦ ፡ ኢበጽሐ ፡ ጊዜሁ ፡ አላ ፡ ኣርእየከ ፡ አምሳለ ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ ወባሕቱ ፡ ዕዲ ፡ ዮርዳኖስ ፡ ወተጠመቅ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ተዐዲ ፡ ወብጻሕ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሳሌም ፡ ወትረክቦ ፡ ለመልከ ፡ ጼዴቅ ፡ ወአነ ፡ እኤዝዞ ፡ ያርኢከ ፡ ተኣምሪሁ ፡ ወአምሳሊሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-said-to-him God, 'No; not-has-arrived his-time, but I-will-show-you likeness-of his-coming. And-but cross(?) Jordan and-be-baptized while you-cross(?) and-arrive (at) city-of Salem and-you-will-find Melchizedek, and-I I-will-command-him that-he-show-you his-wonders and-his-likenesses.'
sentences.i: And God said to him, 'No; his time has not yet come, but I will show you a likeness of his coming. Cross the Jordan and be baptized as you cross, and come to the city of Salem, and you will find Melchizedek; and I will command him to show you his wonders and his likenesses.'
sentences.n: God answers; the speaker is God, the addressee Abraham (ወይቤሎ 'and he said to him', ብህለ + -ሎ). አልቦ 'there is not' as a reply 'no'. ኢበጽሐ 'has not arrived' (3ms perfect). ኣርእየከ is read as 1cs imperfect of አርአየ 'show', 'I will show you' (?); the spelling with the 4th-order ኣ and the እ is unusual (I would expect አርኢከ, cf. ያርኢከ below), but a past 'I showed' does not suit the context. ዕዲ is read as an imperative of ዐደወ 'cross' (?), and ተዐዲ after እንዘ 'while' as 2ms imperfect 'while you cross' (?), though it may be a repeated imperative. Both are guessed from the sense: for a III-w verb I would expect the 2ms imperative ዕዱ and the 2ms imperfect ትዒዱ, so the printed -ዲ endings are irregular (ዕዲ would be 2fs by form); ተጠመቅ 'be baptized' (tä-stem imperative); ብጻሕ imperative 'arrive', its object ሀገረ ሳሌም in the accusative/construct. The baptism of Abraham is the author's own motif. ትረክቦ 2ms imperfect 'you will find him'; እኤዝዞ 1cs 'I will command him'; ያርኢከ 3ms subjunctive 'that he show you'. ተኣምሪሁ ወአምሳሊሁ: ተአምር 'wonder, sign' and አምሳል 'likeness' with the suffix in -ሪሁ/-ሊሁ, which I read as plural 'his wonders, his likenesses' (?); the 'his' could be Melchizedek's or that of ምጽአቱ above. Genesis 14:18 names Melchizedek king of Salem; ለመልከ ጼዴቅ is written as two words in the edition, with ለ- marking the object.

sentences.t: ወገብረ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ወረከቦ ፡ ለመልከ ፡ ጼዴቅ ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ምሥጢረ ፡ ኅብስት ፡ ወወይን ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ዘተገብረ ፡ በፋሲካነ ፡ ለመድኀኒትነ ፡ በእግዚእነ ፡ ኢየሱስ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ዝኬ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ተምኔቱ ፡ ወትፍሥሕቱ ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ ዐዊዶ ፡ ምሥዋዐ ፡ ዘገብረ ፡ መልከ ፡ ጼዴቅ ፡ ነሢኦ ፡ ጸበርተ ፡ ወበቀልተ ፡ በዕለተ ፡ ሰንበት ፤
sentences.l: And-he-did likewise and-found Melchizedek, and-gave-him mystery-of bread and-wine, that-which was-done at-our-Passover of-our-savior, in-our-Lord Jesus Christ. This-indeed(?) he (was) his-desire and-his-joy, of-Abraham, having-circled(?) altar which made Melchizedek, having-taken [ጸበርተ; unknown] and-herbs(?) on-day-of Sabbath;
sentences.i: And he did so, and found Melchizedek, and Melchizedek gave him the mystery of bread and wine — that which was done at the Passover of our Savior, in our Lord Jesus Christ. This was Abraham's desire and joy, as he went about the altar that Melchizedek had made, taking ṣäbärtä (a word I cannot place; perhaps a kind of bread or cake) and herbs(?) on the day of the Sabbath;
sentences.n: Genesis 14:18 (Melchizedek brings out bread and wine) is read as a type of the Eucharist; ምሥጢር 'mystery' also means 'sacrament', and Passover (ፋሲካ) is the Christian Pascha. ውእቱ ዘተገብረ 'that which was done' (ዘ- relative + passive ተገብረ). ዝኬ (?) taken as the demonstrative ዝ + an enclitic -ኬ that I cannot identify ('indeed' is a placeholder guess; the same ending is in በተአምኖኬ, next unit); ውእቱ is the copula. በፋሲካነ ለመድኀኒትነ: ለ- is taken as the genitive marker after an anticipating suffix, as in ምጽአቱ ለወልደ above ('our Passover, that of our Savior'); 'for our Savior' is also possible. ተምኔቱ 'his desire' (ተምኔት + -ሁ) and ትፍሥሕቱ 'his joy', with ለአብርሃም marking the owner. ዐዊዶ (?) is read as a converb 'having encircled, gone around'; the shape fits the converb of a II-w verb (like ቀዊሞ of ቆመ), whose perfect would be ዖደ (a dictionary form I have not checked), but the sense is doubtful; ምሥዋዐ accusative 'altar'. ነሢኦ 'having taken' (converb of ነሥአ). ጸበርተ (?): I cannot place this word (a feminine noun in the accusative); l leaves it untranslated, and i offers only that it may be a kind of bread or cake, a guess from the context; ወበቀልተ (?) is read as ወ- + በቀልት 'herbs, vegetables' (accusative). The Sabbath detail is the author's own; the clause ends with ፤ though the sentence continues.

sentences.t: በተአምኖኬ ፡ ከመ ፡ ተፈሥሐ ፡ ርኢ ፡ ወበተአምኖ ፡ ጸድቀ ፡ ርኢ ፤
sentences.l: By-faith-indeed(?) how he-rejoiced, see; and-by-faith he-was-justified, see;
sentences.i: By faith — see how he rejoiced; and by faith — see — he was made righteous;
sentences.n: The author turns to the reader. ርኢ is a 2ms imperative of ርእየ 'see', here a rhetorical 'look!'. በተአምኖኬ: በ- 'by' + ተአምኖ 'faith, confession' (from አምነ) + -ኬ, an enclitic I cannot identify ('indeed' is a placeholder; see ዝኬ, unit 4). No pronoun is printed, so 'by faith', with Abraham understood. ጸድቀ ርኢ: ጸድቀ is the 3ms perfect 'he was justified', with ርኢ following as in the first clause (ተፈሥሐ ርኢ). 'See righteousness' would need the accusative noun ጽድቀ (6th order), which is not what is printed, so I do not take it. The pairing echoes the justification of Abraham by faith (Genesis 15:6) without quoting it.

sentences.t: ኦአይሁዳዊ ፡ ዕዉር ፡ እንዘ ፡ ብከ ፡ አዕይንተ ፡ ኢትሬኢ ፡ ወእንዘ ፡ ብከ ፡ እዝ ፡ ነ ፡ ኢትሰምዕ ፤
sentences.l: O-Jew, blind one, while to-you eyes you-do-not-see, and-while to-you ears [እዝ ነ; sic] you-do-not-hear;
sentences.i: O Jew, blind man, though you have eyes you do not see, and though you have ears you do not hear;
sentences.n: ኦአይሁዳዊ (?) is written as one word: ኦ 'O' (vocative particle) + አይሁዳዊ 'Jew'. ዕዉር 'blind'. ብከ 'you have' (ቦ + -ከ, the existential way of saying 'have'). እዝ ነ is two words in the edition; I read it as እዝነ, the accusative of እዝን 'ear' used collectively (the plural is አእዛን), wrongly divided in the edition and kept as printed, since the parallel with አዕይንተ 'eyes' calls for it. It is not the suffix -ነ 'our' of the known entry ነ. ኢትሬኢ 'you do not see' and ኢትሰምዕ 'you do not hear' are 2ms imperfect negatives; the Jew is addressed in the singular.

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ በእንቲአክሙ ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ዖሩ ፡ አዕይንቲሆሙ ፡ ወተጸለለ ፡ ልቦሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይለብዉ ፡ ወኢይሣህሎሙ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: As said concerning-you Isaiah prophet, 'They-were-blind(?) their-eyes and-was-overshadowed(?) their-heart, that-not they-understand and-not he-have-mercy-on-them(?)'
sentences.i: As Isaiah the prophet said about you: 'Their eyes grew blind and their heart was darkened, so that they should not understand and He should not have mercy on them.'
sentences.n: Allusion to Isaiah 6:10 (the hardening of the heart; compare John 12:40), as the author remembers and applies it, not a verbatim quotation. በእንቲአክሙ 'concerning you (plural)' (በእንተ + -ክሙ); the address passes from the singular Jew of the last unit to a plural 'you'. ዖሩ (?) is read as the 3mp perfect of a II-w verb ዖረ 'be blind' (like ሖሩ of ሖረ), intransitive, 'they were blind, grew blind'; the lexeme is from memory and unchecked. ተጸለለ (?) 'was overshadowed' (tä-stem; as I recall the verb means 'shade, overshadow'); 'darkened' is the sense the context asks for. ልቦሙ is singular, 'their heart'. ከመ ኢይለብዉ 'that they not understand' (3mp subjunctive, as with ኢትሌቡ above; the spelling here is regular). ወኢይሣህሎሙ (?): ይሣህሎሙ read as a 3ms subjunctive 'he have mercy' with -ሎሙ 'to them', 'and that He (God, presumably) not have mercy on them'; the verb form and the subject are uncertain. The part ends with the run of ፨ marks, closing the chapter.
